ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic gems and fiery blues, with standout Lovelight & Viola Lee
ai_show_review.blurb: The early‑show opens with a flawless acoustic set highlighted by Deep Elem Blues and an alternate‑lyric Friend of the Devil. The electric half builds into a scorching Lovelight and raunchy Viola Lee Blues, while Cold Rain & Snow showcases a crisp Jerry solo. Overall performance is strong despite some tape glitches and low organ level.
ai_show_review.review: March 20, 1970 at the Capitol Theater captures the Dead in a transitional moment – an acoustic‑driven first set that flows into a blues‑heavy electric second half. The cleaned‑up soundboard (gd1970-03-20.sbd.smith) reveals crisp folk numbers like Deep Elem Blues and a playful take on Friend of the Devil with alternate lyrics, then erupts into a scorching Lovelight where Pigpen’s low‑in‑the‑mix organ is compensated by his priceless rap. Viola Lee Blues roars with raw energy, while the later Cold Rain & Snow delivers a “nice solo” that reviewers singled out even on the muddier matrix source. Good Lovin’ holds its own despite occasional tape cuts, and the overall pacing remains engaging, making this show a solid snapshot of the early ’70 Dead sound.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with good transfer; clear acoustic separation and captures the key moments despite minor tape glitches.

key_highlights: Stellar acoustic opening featuring Deep Elem Blues and alternate‑lyric Friend of the Devil
Scorching Lovelight with Pigpen’s memorable rap
Raunchy Viola Lee Blues that drive the second half
Jerry’s standout solo on Cold Rain & Snow

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers solid leads throughout, highlighted by a crisp solo on Cold Rain & Snow and tight guitar work in both acoustic and electric sections.
band_performance.Phil: Sings loudly and on key with high harmonies that are occasionally buried; provides a reliable bass foundation across the set.
